title: Brushy Creek Vote & Meeting Revamp
summary:
*   The city council voted 3-4 against continuing the **Brushy Creek Project**, effectively halting its progress.
*   Discussions focused on **revising meeting procedures**, including setting new Tuesday meeting hours (3:00 PM - 7:00 PM), dedicating the first Tuesday of each month for board appointments, and considering 5:00 PM for zoning hearings.
*   The necessity of **speaker sign-in cards** for public meetings was questioned as part of an effort to streamline discussions.

!
Motion - FAILED
Councilmember Carl-Mitchell made a motion, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Shipman to stay with
the Brushy Creek Project. Motion FAILED by a vote of 3-4, Mayor Cooke, Councilmembers
Humphrey and Nofziger voted No.
COUNCIL MEETINGS
Barustone
Mayor Cooke introduced an item to Council to discuss procedures and policies and other
related issues relating to how City Council meetings are conducted. Mayor Cooke said the
Tuesday meetings will begin at 3:00P.M. and last no later than 7:00P.M. He said the first
Tuesday of each month should be set for board and commission appointments. Mayor Pro Tem
Shipman said Council should be notified when dignitaries are going to be present in the
Council Chamber to receive proclamations.
There was also discussion concerning the setting of zoning hearings at 5:00 P.M. and Mayor
Pro Tem Shipman also questioned the necessity of sign-in cards for speakers at the
meetings. She thought that took up too much time.
ADJOURNMENT - Council adjourned its meeting at 6:15 P.M.
